conventions.convention: Inner products and sesquilinear forms are linear in the first variable; P_g f = ⟨f,g⟩g.
The representing Hamiltonian satisfies q(u,v)=⟨H_q u,v⟩; the associated generator in the e^{tA} convention is A=−H_q.
The local rank-one resolvent is (H−zI)^{-1}, opposite in sign to the cited general library definition (zI−H)^{-1}. The local formula explicitly fixes its convention.
Fourier transformation uses exp(−2πix·ξ); −Δ has multiplier 4π²|ξ|², operator domain W^{2,2}, and form domain W^{1,2}.
Min-max indices start at k=1; eigenvalues are counted with multiplicity. The bottom of an empty essential spectrum and an infimum over an empty variational family are +∞.
Birman–Schwinger counting uses eigenvalues of H strictly below −κ² and eigenvalues of K_κ strictly greater than 1; equality is handled separately by the eigenspace correspondence.
All eight assigned statements assume AC and Countable Choice. The separable example uses the momentum multiplier |p|² directly, rather than the spatial Fourier multiplier 4π²|ξ|².
For the attractive Gaussian separable model, a negative eigenvalue exists exactly when 1+λI_0<0; equality yields no negative eigenvalue.

load_bearing.statement: Under AC and Countable Choice, a densely defined symmetric form q bounded below by −c and complete in q[u]+(c+1)‖u‖² has a unique self-adjoint representing operator H_q≥−cI, with D((H_q+cI)^{1/2})=Q and the stated representability characterization of D(H_q). A symmetric perturbation satisfying |v[u,u]|≤a q_0[u]+b‖u‖², 0≤a<1, of a nonnegative closed form remains closed on the same domain and bounded below by −b.

Under AC and Countable Choice, on L²(R³;C) with the negative-sign 2π Fourier convention, the weak-gradient form on W^{1,2} is dense, symmetric, nonnegative and closed. Its associated self-adjoint operator is −Δ with domain W^{2,2}, and D((−Δ)^{1/2})=W^{1,2}.

Under AC and Countable Choice, for nonzero complex H and self-adjoint A≥−cI, the infimum over k-dimensional subspaces of Q(A) of the maximum unit-vector form value is the kth eigenvalue below α=inf σ_ess(A), counted with multiplicity, when at least k such eigenvalues exist; otherwise it equals α. Compact inclusion of the form domain implies a complete orthonormal eigenbasis, finite eigenvalue multiplicities and accumulation only at +∞.

Under AC, for lower-semibounded self-adjoint H_0, g∈H and real λ, H_λ=H_0+λP_g is self-adjoint on D(H_0). For z∈ρ(H_0) with d_λ(z)=1+λ⟨R_0(z)g,g⟩≠0, its resolvent is R_0(z)−λR_0(z)P_gR_0(z)/d_λ(z). For real E<inf σ(H_0) and g≠0, E is an eigenvalue exactly when d_λ(E)=0, and its eigenspace is one-dimensional.
Under AC and Countable Choice, for κ>0, G_κ(x)=exp(−κ|x|)/(4π|x|) off the origin belongs to L¹∩L² and has Fourier transform (4π²|ξ|²+κ²)^{-1}. Convolution by G_κ is (−Δ+κ²)^{-1} on L².

Under AC and Countable Choice, for measurable nonnegative essentially bounded W vanishing almost everywhere outside a compact set, H=−Δ−M_W is self-adjoint and bounded below. For κ>0, K_κ=M_s(−Δ+κ²I)^{-1}M_s, s=√W, is positive self-adjoint compact with the stated Yukawa kernel. Its eigenspace at 1 is isomorphic to the eigenspace of H at −κ², and its finite eigenvalue count above 1 equals the finite eigenvalue count of H strictly below −κ², with multiplicities.

concerns.concern: Step 4.2 concludes that T is compact because it is an operator-norm limit of finite-rank maps P_nT. This uses finite-rank compactness and closure of compact operators under norm limits without an explicit supplier or local argument in this item. The claim is valid under its Countable Choice and Hilbert-space hypotheses, but the justification must be reconstructed.
